L4@P0: By Valery Alexeev
L5@P0: Abstract
L6@P0: I prove the existence, and describe the structure, of moduli space of pairs
L7@P0: (P, Θ) consisting of a projective variety P with semiabelian group action and
L8@P0: an ample Cartier divisor on it satisfying a few simple conditions. Every connected component of this moduli space is proper. A component containing a
L9@P0: projective toric variety is described by a configuration of several polytopes, the
L10@P0: main one of which is the secondary polytope. On the other hand, the component containing a principally polarized abelian variety provides a moduli
L11@P0: compactification of Ag. The main irreducible component of this compactification is described by an “infinite periodic” analog of the secondary polytope
L12@P0: and coincides with the toroidal compactification of Ag for the second Voronoi
L13@P0: decomposition.

L72@P1: Introduction
L73@P1: In this paper I construct a proper moduli stack and its coarse moduli
L74@P1: space, also proper, of pairs (P, Θ), where P is a reduced projective scheme
L75@P1: with a semiabelian group action and Θ is a Cartier divisor. The pairs should
L76@P1-2: satisfy a few simple conditions. For me, the motivation for considering moduliCOMPLETE MODULI 613
L77@P2: of such pairs came from the log minimal model program; see [Ale2]. However,
L78@P2: the minimal model program in dimensions ≥ 4 remains conjectural, and so in
L79@P2: this paper I do not use it.
L80@P2: When the group acting on our variety is a torus and the sheaf OP (Θ) is
L81@P2: linearized, our theory is closely related to the Gelfand-Kapranov-Zelevinsky
L82@P2: study of families of cycles and their toric degenerations; see [GKZ] and references there. (The cycles appear as images of our pairs under a natural projection to P
L83@P2: n
L84@P2: .) The notions of regular decompositions and secondary polytopes
L85@P2: defined there play an important role in our study. It turns out the closure of
L86@P2: the stratum containing the standard projective toric variety P[Q] for a lattice
L87@P2: polytope Q is itself the projective toric variety corresponding to the secondary
L88@P2: polytope Σ(Q). Examination of the other strata in our moduli space naturally
L89@P2: leads to definition of the generalized secondary polytopes for each subdivision
L90@P2: of Q. I describe an explicit stratification on the space and compute the dimensions of the strata. Their exact configuration depends on the resolution of
L91@P2: the so-called generalized Baues problem in geometric combinatorics. (I thank
L92@P2: Professor Sturmfels for pointing out this connection to me.)
L93@P2: One of the most interesting strata in our moduli space is the one corresponding to abelian torsors with a divisor defining principal polarization. This
L94@P2: stratum can be naturally identified with Ag, the moduli of principally polarized
